intro: The verbs of a life: being born, growing up, marrying, retiring. All of them in the indefinido.
p.nací.consejo: Nacer in the past is «nací», «naciste», «nació». With a soft c: «na-THI» in Spain.
p.crecí.consejo: Crecer is regular in the indefinido: «crecí», «creciste», «creció». It goes well with «en» and a place.
p.me casé.consejo: Casarse takes «se» in front: yo «me casé», ella «se casó». The person goes with «con».
p.se casaron.consejo: It is the ellos form. With a single person it is «se casó».
p.se divorció.consejo: Divorciarse also takes «se». It is written with a v in the middle: di-vor-ciar.
p.tuvieron.consejo: Tener is irregular in the indefinido: «tuve», «tuvo», «tuvieron». It has no accent.
p.se jubiló.consejo: Jubilarse means to stop working because of age. «Se jubiló» has an accent on the last o.
p.el bebé.consejo: You say «el bebé» for a boy or a girl. The accent is on the last e.
p.el adolescente.consejo: For a girl: «la adolescente». The word does not change, only the article.
p.el adulto.consejo: The feminine is «la adulta». It is written with d and u.
p.la persona mayor.consejo: «Persona mayor» is kind and respectful. It is always feminine, even for a man.
p.la infancia.consejo: You say «en mi infancia». The c sounds «th» in Spain: «in-FAN-thya».
p.la juventud.consejo: The j sounds like a strong h: «hu-ben-TUD». You say «en mi juventud».
p.la pareja.consejo: It is feminine for a man or a woman: «mi pareja». It also means two people together.
p.a los treinta años.consejo: For age use «a los» and the number: «a los veinte años».
p.de niño.consejo: A girl says «de niña». «De niño» is used to talk about the past.
p.de joven.consejo: It does not change for boy or girl: «de joven». It is used to talk about the past.
b1.texto:
Use the **indefinido** to tell the finished events of a life: **nací**, **crecí**, **estudié**, **me casé**, **tuve** un hijo, **me jubilé**, **murió**.

- **¿Dónde naciste?** → **Nací en** Sevilla.
- For an age use **a los … años**: **me casé a los treinta años**.
- For a year use **en**: **en 1990**.
- **Casarse con** someone: **se casó con una médica**.

The stages: **la infancia**, **la juventud**; **un bebé**, **un niño**, **un adolescente**, **un adulto**, **una persona mayor**. **De niño** and **de joven** mean «when I was a child» and «when I was young».
b2.f1.texto: I was born in Seville, but I grew up in Madrid.
b2.f2.texto: When did your parents get married?
b2.f3.texto: They got married in 1990 and had two children.
b3.titulo: Stages and events of a life
b4.texto:
Each fact of a life takes its own small word:

- Age: **a los** + number + **años**: **a los veinte años**.
- Year: **en**: **en 1990**.
- Place: **en**: **nací en Sevilla**.
- The person you marry: **con**: **me casé con una médica**.
- How long ago: **hace** + time: **murió hace diez años**.

**Estar casado** describes how someone is now; **casarse** tells the moment it happened. **De niño** and **de joven** place the memory in a stage of life.
b4.e1.texto: As a child I lived in a small city.
b5.f0.texto: I was born in a white house with a flower courtyard.
b5.f1.texto: The smell of the orange trees filled my childhood.
b5.f2.texto: My grandmother sang old songs beside the well.
b5.f3.texto: I grew up under a blue and bright sky.
b5.f4.texto: The afternoon light painted the courtyard walls gold.
b5.f5.texto: As a young person I travelled to Madrid with a small suitcase.
b5.f6.texto: The train crossed golden fields under the light of dawn.
b5.f7.texto: In the new city I found a quiet job.
b5.f8.texto: I got married at thirty on a sunny morning.
b5.f9.texto: Afterwards my daughter was born with dark eyes.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Cuándo» asks about the moment, not the place.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That asks about the present: you live, not you were born.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «Dónde» asks for the place and «naciste» is the birth.
b6.pregunta: What do you ask to learn the birthplace?
b7.frase: Mi tía se casó ____ los veinte años.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «En» goes with calendar years: en 1990. For age you need «a».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Con» introduces the person you marry, not the age.
b7.pregunta: Which word goes before the age?
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is «se casó». «Se jubiló» is about work.
b9.o1: Dejó de trabajar por la edad
b9.o1.refuerzo: Correct: jubilarse is to stop working because of age.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That is «nació». Jubilarse has nothing to do with being born.
b10.frase: Mi primo se casó ____ una médica.
b10.o0.refuerzo: «De» does not introduce the partner with this verb.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «A» does not work here: casarse needs «con».
b10.o2.refuerzo: Well done! Casarse always goes with «con» plus the person.
b10.pregunta: Which word does the verb casarse need?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Where were you born?» (tú)
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: a calendar year goes with «en».
b12.o1.refuerzo: «A» is for age, not for the year.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Con» goes with people: you marry someone.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence puts the year correctly?
p.naciste.consejo: For «tú» the past in -er verbs ends in -iste, with no accent: «naciste». The c sounds «th» in Spain.
p.tía.consejo: The accent on the í separates the vowels: TI-a. The uncle is «tío».
p.casó.consejo: It is used with «se»: «se casó con una médica». The person goes with «con».
p.patio.consejo: «Io» is one syllable: PA-tyo. Courtyards with flowers are typical of southern Spain.
p.naranjos.consejo: A tree and its fruit have related names: «naranjo» (tree) and «naranja» (fruit). The j sounds like a strong h.
p.abuela.consejo: The grandfather is «abuelo». «Ue» is one syllable: a-BWE-la. The b sounds b.
p.antiguas.consejo: It agrees with «canciones»: feminine plural. The u in «gua» is pronounced: an-TI-gwas.
p.pozo.consejo: The z sounds «th» in Spain: PO-tho. It is masculine: «el pozo».
p.pintó.consejo: «Pintar de oro» means to paint something gold. The accent marks the past: «pintó».
p.muros.consejo: «Muro» is a wall around a space, such as a courtyard or a city; «pared» is the wall inside a room.
p.viajé.consejo: The j sounds like a strong h and the v sounds b: bya-HE. The accent marks the last syllable.
p.cruzó.consejo: The z sounds «th» in Spain: kru-THO. Before e it becomes c: «crucé».
p.dorados.consejo: It comes from «oro» (gold). It agrees with «campos»: masculine plural. The d is always soft, never «th».
p.encontré.consejo: In the present «encontrar» changes (encuentro), but the past «encontré» keeps the o. The accent marks the last syllable.
p.primo.consejo: It ends in -o, so it is masculine. Its feminine form is «prima».
